# package od

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/od"
```

Package od is the CANopen object dictionary (CiA 301 7.4): objects addressed by a 16-bit index and an 8-bit sub-index, with data types, access rights, PDO mappability, default values and limits.

A [Dictionary](#type-dictionary) distinguishes two kinds of access. Remote accesses ([Dictionary.Read](#func-dictionary-read), [Dictionary.Write](#func-dictionary-write)) come from the bus (an SDO server, a received PDO): they obey the access rights and limits and call the hooks, and refuse with an [canopen.AbortCode](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortCode) that an SDO server sends unchanged. Local accesses ([Dictionary.Get](#func-dictionary-get), [Dictionary.Set](#func-dictionary-set)) come from the application: they bypass access rights but still check the data type. Watchers see every successful change of either kind.

A Dictionary is safe for concurrent use. Hooks and watchers run without the dictionary lock held, so they may access the dictionary.

### type Access

```go

```

Access is the access right of a sub-object.

```go
const (
	AccessRO    Access = iota + 1 // read only; the value may change
	AccessWO                      // write only
	AccessRW                      // read and write
	AccessRWR                     // read and write, mapped in a TPDO (process input)
	AccessRWW                     // read and write, mapped in an RPDO (process output)
	AccessConst                   // read only, the value never changes
)
```

### type Dictionary

```go
type Dictionary struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Dictionary is an object dictionary with the current values of its sub-objects.

#### func New

```go
func New(node canopen.NodeID) *Dictionary
```

New returns an empty dictionary for a node; node-ID-relative defaults use the node-ID (which may be 0 when not known yet, see SetNodeID).

#### func Standard

```go
func Standard(cfg Config) (*Dictionary, error)
```

Standard returns a dictionary with the communication profile objects of cfg, in their CiA 301 default configuration: 0x1000, 0x1001, 0x1005, 0x1006, 0x1007, 0x1014, 0x1015, 0x1017, 0x1018, 0x1019, 0x1200 always; the others as cfg selects. PDO COB-IDs follow the predefined connection set for PDOs 1..4 (valid) and are invalid (bit 31) beyond. Add the application objects to the result.

#### func (Dictionary) Add

```go
func (d *Dictionary) Add(o *Object) error
```

Add adds an object and sets its values to their defaults. It checks the object: sub-objects sorted and unique, a VAR with exactly sub-index 0, known data types, defaults and limits of the right size.

#### func (Dictionary) HookCount

```go
func (d *Dictionary) HookCount() int
```

HookCount returns the number of read hooks, write hooks and watchers registered on the dictionary. It is a diagnostic: services remove what they register when they are closed, so the count of a dictionary that nodes are repeatedly created on and closed stays stable.

#### func (Dictionary) OnRead

```go
func (d *Dictionary) OnRead(index uint16, sub int, h ReadHook) (remove func())
```

OnRead registers a read hook for a sub-object, or for every sub-object of the index when sub is -1. Hooks run in registration order; the more specific (sub ≥ 0) hooks run first. The returned function removes the hook.

#### func (Dictionary) OnWrite

```go
func (d *Dictionary) OnWrite(index uint16, sub int, h WriteHook) (remove func())
```

OnWrite registers a write hook for a sub-object, or for every sub-object of the index when sub is -1. The returned function removes the hook.

```go
func (d *Dictionary) Read(index uint16, sub uint8) ([]byte, error)
```

Read is a remote read: it checks the access right, calls the read hooks and returns a copy of the value.

```go
func (d *Dictionary) Remove(index uint16)
```

Remove deletes an object; hooks registered for it stay.

#### func (Dictionary) Reset

```go
func (d *Dictionary) Reset(from, to uint16)
```

Reset restores the defaults of every object with an index in \[from, to], as an NMT reset does (communication: 0x1000..0x1FFF; application: 0x2000..0x9FFF). Watchers are notified of values that changed.

#### func (Dictionary) Set

```go
func (d *Dictionary) Set(index uint16, sub uint8, data []byte) error
```

Set is a local write: it checks the data type length (not the access right, limits or hooks), stores the value and notifies the watchers.

#### func (Dictionary) SetNodeID

```go
func (d *Dictionary) SetNodeID(node canopen.NodeID)
```

SetNodeID changes the node-ID node-ID-relative defaults use. It does not change current values: call [Dictionary.Reset](#func-dictionary-reset) afterwards, as a reset communication does.

### type Object

```go
type Object struct {
	Index uint16
	Name  string
	Type  ObjectType
	// Subs are the sub-objects in ascending sub-index order. Records may
	// have gaps.
	Subs []*Variable
}
```

Object is one entry of the dictionary: a VAR (one sub-object, sub-index 0), an ARRAY or a RECORD (sub-index 0 holding the highest sub-index, and the sub-objects), or a DOMAIN.

#### func NewArray

```go
func NewArray(index uint16, name string, dt canopen.DataType, access Access, n int, def any, sub0Access Access) *Object
```

NewArray returns an ARRAY object with n elements of one type, named "\<name> \<i>", and sub-index 0 (number of elements, UNSIGNED8) with the access sub0Access. A negative n gives no elements; above 255 elements the sub-indices repeat and [Dictionary.Add](#func-dictionary-add) rejects the object.

#### func NewRecord

```go
func NewRecord(index uint16, name string, subs ...*Variable) *Object
```

NewRecord returns a RECORD object with the sub-objects, sorted by the caller. Sub-index 0 (highest sub-index supported, UNSIGNED8, ro) is added unless subs has one.

#### func NewVar

```go
func NewVar(index uint16, name string, dt canopen.DataType, access Access, def any) *Object
```

NewVar returns a VAR object. def as for [Sub](#func-sub).

#### func PDOObjects

```go
func PDOObjects(transmit bool, n, entries int) (comm, mapping *Object)
```

PDOObjects returns the communication and mapping parameter objects of TPDO (transmit) or RPDO n (1..512) in their default configuration. An n outside 1..512 gets the indices of PDO 1.

### type ReadHook

```go
type ReadHook func(v *Variable, stored []byte) ([]byte, error)
```

ReadHook is called on a remote read of a sub-object with its stored value; it returns the value to deliver (e.g. a value computed on demand). Returning an error (preferably an [canopen.AbortCode](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortCode)) refuses the read.

### type Variable

```go
type Variable struct {
	Index    uint16
	SubIndex uint8
	Name     string
	DataType canopen.DataType
	Access   Access
	// PDOMappable allows mapping into a PDO.
	PDOMappable bool
	// Default is the encoded default value. When NodeIDRelative is true
	// the node-ID is added to it (EDS "$NODEID+..." defaults); Add
	// refuses a default to which node-ID 127 cannot be added without
	// leaving the type.
	Default        []byte
	NodeIDRelative bool
	// Low and High are optional encoded inclusive limits for numeric
	// types; nil means no limit.
	Low, High []byte
	// MaxSize bounds the length of a variable-length value (strings,
	// DOMAIN); 0 means unbounded.
	MaxSize int
}
```

Variable is one sub-object: the unit an SDO transfers and a PDO maps. Its fields describe it; the current value is held by the [Dictionary](#type-dictionary) it belongs to. Do not change the fields of a Variable once it has been added to a dictionary.

#### func Sub

```go
func Sub(sub uint8, name string, dt canopen.DataType, access Access, def any) *Variable
```

Sub returns a sub-object description for [NewRecord](#func-newrecord) and [NewArray](#func-newarray); its Index is filled in by them. def is a Go value encoded with dt ([canopen.Encode](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#Encode)), or nil for a zero default.

#### func (Variable) Key

```go
func (v *Variable) Key() string
```

Key returns "IIII:SS", the index and sub-index in hexadecimal.

### type Watcher

```go
type Watcher func(v *Variable, data []byte)
```

Watcher is called after a value changed, by a remote or a local write.

### type WriteHook

```go
type WriteHook func(v *Variable, data []byte) error
```

WriteHook is called on a remote write of a sub-object before the value is stored, after the access, length and limit checks. Returning an error (preferably an [canopen.AbortCode](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortCode)) refuses the write.
